subject: SIG follow-up: memory segmentation, eviction behavior, and evidence request
messages:

Cc: Matt Ramirez <matt.ramirez@auditorlab.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: SIG follow-up: memory segmentation & eviction behavior

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the SIG package you sent last week. Acme's security team had two follow-ups that are blocking our internal review: they want more concrete evidence around how Redwood Dedicated handles GPU memory segmentation and eviction during preemption/bursting events. Specifically:

- Threat model: can you describe the attack surface for cross-tenant memory exposure (e.g., buffer reuse, stale KV cache entries, page-table leakage)?
- Eviction behavior: empirical logs showing preemption/eviction counts and how KV cache residency is enforced when multiple tenants share a host or during cold-starts.
- Artefacts: a short architecture diagram, a sample log showing an eviction event (redacted), and the template attestation that your compliance org would sign.

We need these items to finalize the SIG review by Oct 26. Is that timeline feasible? If useful, we'd be open to a 30-minute technical run-through next week.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Clarke
Security Lead, Acme Energy
Sophie.Clarke@acme-energy.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: memory segmentation & eviction behavior

Hi Sophie,

Appreciate the clear asks. We've looped in Marcus (serving runtime) and Hannah (security/compliance) to provide the technical artefacts and the attestation template. High-level answers up-front:

- Threat model: Redwood Dedicated uses strict process and kernel-level isolation for inference workers; GPU memory is not shared between tenant processes. We enforce per-tenant allocation and tear-down of NVidia contexts; KV cache is per-tenant process and cleared on session teardown or eviction.
- Eviction behavior: We instrument NVML and our runtime telemetry to record preemption/eviction events. We can produce a small redacted sample CSV showing eviction timestamps, tenant id (hashed), and pre/post-KV cache residency sizes.
- Evidence: attaching a top-level architecture diagram and a sample log extract. Hannah will share the attestation template and propose redaction guidance for logs.

Can Marcus provide the deeper technical threat model doc and the specific log sample by Friday? We'll aim to have the attestation draft signed next week.

Next steps:
1) Marcus: technical deep-dive + eviction metric sample (ETA: Oct 17)
2) Hannah: attestation template + redaction plan (ETA: Oct 18)
3) Priya: coordinate a 30-min runbook walk (if Acme wants a demo)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_memory_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf (pdf, 72KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@acme-energy.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SIG follow-up: memory segmentation & eviction behavior

Hi Sophie — following up with the technical detail and the sample metrics you requested. Summary first, then artefacts.

Summary (technical):
- Physical/GPU memory separation: We allocate a dedicated CUDA context per inference worker. Contexts map to distinct GPU virtual address spaces; there is no mechanism in our runtime to share raw device pointers across tenant processes. We rely on the GPU driver's hardware isolation plus our process lifecycle management.
- KV cache residency: KV cache is an in-process structure maintained by the runtime; entries are tied to a tenant session identifier and stored in device memory allocated to that process. On session teardown or eviction we zero out device memory and free the allocation before returning resources to the pool.
- Eviction and preemption: For Dedicated hosts we configure preemption windows and use a soft-eviction policy: the runtime will attempt graceful checkpointing of KV state to local encrypted SSD (only when configured) and then force-free memory on timeout. Eviction events increment a telemetry counter exposed via NVML and our Prometheus metrics.
- Monitoring/defense: We track anomalous access patterns (excessive page faults, repeated context creation) and correlate with tenant IDs (hashed). Alerts trigger a host-level quarantine and customer ops escalation.

Attached artefacts (redacted/sample):
- dedicated_gpu_eviction_metrics_20261017.csv (CSV, 42KB) — sample rows: timestamp,host_id,tenant_hash,eviction_type,pre_kv_size_bytes,post_kv_size_bytes
- kvcache_residency_sample.log (log, 18KB) — redacted log lines showing memory zeroing sequence and NVML eviction signals
- redwood_memory_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf (supplied by Priya)

Technical notes for reviewers:
- We do not use MIG in our current Dedicated offering; isolation is achieved at the process/context layer and through strict lifecycle controls.
- We run periodic fuzz tests and side-channel analysis as part of our release verification; results are available under NDA.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Attestation template and redaction guidance

Hi Sophie,

Attached is a short attestation template our compliance team uses to confirm deployment and operational controls for Dedicated customers. A few notes on redaction and sharing logs:

- We will hash tenant identifiers and remove any PII before sharing logs. Hashing is one-way and we can provide a mapping under NDA if needed.
- We remove host names and internal IPs; we keep timestamps, metric counters, and anonymized tenant hashes.
- For very sensitive customers we'll provide a time-limited read-only link to redacted artifacts rather than sending raw files.

Please find the attestation draft attached. If Acme needs an escalated attestation on company letterhead, we can route a signed attestation through our security team — that process typically takes 3 business days after legal review.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: attestation_template_signed.txt (txt, 6KB)

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: memory segmentation, eviction behavior, and evidence request

Thanks all — that looks great and addresses the bulk of our questions. A couple of quick items before we close the SIG: 

- Can you confirm the hashing algorithm used for tenant identifiers and whether you retain the salt? (we prefer SHA-256 with per-host salt)
- We'd like a 30-minute runbook/demo the week of Oct 25 to walk through an eviction event in real time if possible. Please propose 2 slots.
- We'll accept the redacted CSV and logs you mentioned; please confirm ETA for those artefacts (and the signed attestation).

If you can send the ETA and a couple proposed meeting times, I'll loop in Acme's cloud security lead and finalize our internal sign-off. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Cheers,
Sophie
Security Lead, Acme Energy
